overall: The AG found the Millbury Working Group is not a public body under the Open Meeting Law, so the notice, minutes, and quorum allegations were not violations; no remedy was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Group failed to post notice of its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Group is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law, and therefore did not violate the law in the ways alleged.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Group failed to create minutes of its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Group is not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and therefore did not violate the law by failing to post notice or create minutes of meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint suggested two Board of Selectmen members may have taken part in Group meetings, raising a quorum or deliberation concern.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, there is no evidence that a quorum of the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals or other public body participated in the Group or otherwise deliberated outside of a properly posted meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
